mechanism.kind: preventive preflight + environment redirection + post-run mtime watch
mechanism.not: OS/security sandbox that confines subprocess writes

preflight.what: validates paths and configuration before spawning; refuses to start when blockers exist
checks: project is inside the declared sandbox after realpath
sandbox does not overlap the user profile
nearest pnpm-workspace root equals the project (blocks ancestral workspace selection)
packageManager pin is exact and declared on the project (blocks Corepack inheritance)
storeDir/cacheDir/stateDir/globalDir/virtualStoreDir/modulesDir inside the sandbox when set in yaml

environmentRedirection.what: sets TEMP/TMP, XDG_*, pnpm_config_store/cache/state/userconfig and Expo home under the sandbox
environmentRedirection.effect: biases where pnpm and well-behaved tools write by default; does not deny writes elsewhere

subprocessRestrictions.spawn: spawnSync('pnpm', …) with shell on win32; no Node --permission, no job-object write ACL, no AppContainer
subprocessRestrictions.scripts: when ignoreScripts is false, project and dependency lifecycle scripts run with the redirected env only
subprocessRestrictions.network: not restricted by the guard (registry access is required for a real install)
subprocessRestrictions.postRunWatch: compares mtime of a fixed list (ancestor configs, user npmrc, optional extras); detects some changes after the fact; does not prevent them

nodePermissionProbe.status: configuration result, not a general incompatibility claim and not a proof of the substitute
nodePermissionProbe.observed: under Node.js 25.2.1 --permission, a pnpm install attempt failed with ERR_ACCESS_DENIED on getaddrinfo(registry.npmjs.org); the home canary was untouched
nodePermissionProbe.meaning: that run could not reach the registry under the flags used; it does not prove that every permission configuration is incompatible with pnpm, and it does not prove that the guard's env redirection confines writes

blockers: pnpm would use the workspace at <sandbox>\guard-proof\ancestral\sandbox\ancestor, not the project <sandbox>\guard-proof\ancestral\sandbox\ancestor\child
the pnpm version would be inherited from <sandbox>\guard-proof\ancestral\sandbox\ancestor (pnpm@10.27.0)
pnpmfile present (.pnpmfile.cjs): it runs code even with --ignore-scripts

writeProof.claimUnderTest: guard blocks writes outside the sandbox by subprocesses of the install
writeProof.how: project postinstall writes to a sibling folder outside the sandbox but still under the disposable root; ignoreScripts=false so the lifecycle script runs; allowBuilds empty and no dependency builds
stderrTail: Downloading the pnpm 12.5.1 binary for win32-x64...
writeProof.okInterpretation: FAIL as a write-confinement claim: the subprocess wrote outside the sandbox; the guard did not prevent it

limitsOfThisProof: proves a legitimate install can complete under preflight + env redirection with --ignore-scripts
does not prove write confinement of subprocesses

nodeProbeRestatement.priorObservation: Node.js 25.2.1 with --permission: pnpm install failed ERR_ACCESS_DENIED getaddrinfo registry.npmjs.org; home canary unchanged
nodeProbeRestatement.classification: result of that specific permission configuration, not general incompatibility of pnpm with every permission setup, and not evidence that the guard substitutes for it
nodeProbeRestatement.intactCanaryMeaning: an intact canary after a network denial does not prove write confinement of the guard and does not close ancestral-workspace or write-block criteria

installsMayClaim: preflight refuses ancestral workspace / inherited packageManager / unsafe settings before spawn
env redirects default store/cache/temp/xdg into the declared sandbox directory
post-run watch of a fixed file list (detection, not prevention)
installsMustNotClaim: Node permission model as the substitute mechanism
intact canary after network failure as proof of isolation
